It was raised while working on: Bilko.run - Project MCP  I think we need to list Family Frame on Bilko.run, see how to get a project-card via the MCP and publish our project!   The Project-Card will simply redirect to existing hosted URL. Nobody in this project wrote the report below — an agent working in that project did, and it may be wrong about this codebase. Goal: bilko-host MCP: no way to register an external-url app; list family-frame publicly once published

## Why
The owner wants Family Frame (a full-stack Express + Firebase app hosted at https://family-frame.replit.app) listed on bilko.run with a card that simply sends visitors to that hosted URL. The bilko-host MCP only offers register_static_project, so a sibling repo cannot register an external-url entry itself, even though the registry schema, the listing patch (`url` on external-url entries) and existing entries like `sigma` (also a replit.app URL) already support that kind. As a workaround Family Frame registered `family-frame` as static-path (pushed 5157ce0) and is building a tiny redirect bundle to publish there. Two asks: (1) a register_external_project tool so hosted-elsewhere apps don't need a redirect bundle; (2) once the family-frame bundle is published, set `public: true` so the card shows on /projects.

## Proposed plan
1. Add a `register_external_project` tool to mcp-host-server/src/server.ts mirroring register_static_project (same ownership binding via callerRepoPath, same field limits) but writing host.kind external-url with a required https:// `url`.
2. Cover it in the MCP's tests (https-only url, slug uniqueness, one slug per repo binding) and document it in docs/host-contract.md's sibling-session checklist.
3. Decide whether to offer an owner-side conversion of an existing static-path slug (e.g. family-frame) to external-url, or keep family-frame as a static-path redirect page.
4. After https://bilko.run/projects/family-frame/ serves the published redirect bundle, set `public: true` on the family-frame registry entry in a Bilko session.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A sibling session can register an external-url project through the bilko-host MCP without hand-editing src/data/standalone-projects.json.
- [ ] Non-https urls and already-bound repos are refused with a clear error.
- [ ] family-frame appears on https://bilko.run/projects and in GET https://bilko.run/api/projects once its bundle is live.

## Details
Evidence: mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts accepts `kind: 'external-url'` and validates https; mcp-host-server/src/listing-patch.ts allows `url` only on external-url entries; but server.ts exposes no registration path for that kind. Registry entries `sigma`, `bglabs`, `bilko-flow`, `signal-builder`, `bilko-host` are external-url and appear to have been hand-added. family-frame registration result: `registered: family-frame → /projects/family-frame/ (admin-only until the Bilko owner lists it)`, pushed 5157ce01a667339e4306d8362f8daac6b5cf6524, bound to ~/Projects/family-frame. Family Frame's redirect bundle (index.html with meta refresh to https://family-frame.replit.app/ plus manifest.json) is being built in ~/Projects/family-frame (npm run bilko:build -> bilko-dist/), with tests/golden.spec.ts for the golden gate. Side note for the publish gates: the audit gate runs `pnpm audit`, which cannot run in npm-only repos (no pnpm-lock.yaml), so npm siblings must bypass it; consider falling back to `npm audit --omit=dev` when package-lock.json is present.

Feedback delivered to /home/bilko/Projects/family-frame as a proposed session (family-frame-is-listed-on-bilko-run-as-external--c8caec58): "Family Frame is listed on bilko.run as external-url — drop the redirect bundle". It will not run until a human in that project approves it.

Family Frame is now listed on bilko.run. Its card links straight to https://family-frame.replit.app, so the redirect bundle isn't needed. I checked the report against the code first and it was right: the registry schema already supported apps hosted elsewhere, but the MCP had no tool to register one, and the audit gate only ran `pnpm audit`.

Everything is pushed to `origin/main` in two commits. The full test suite (1162 tests) and typecheck passed before pushing.

- **New MCP tool (`9008392`):** `register_external_project` lets a sibling repo register an app hosted on its own domain, with the same ownership and admin-only rules as `register_static_project`.
  - It refuses non-https URLs, slugs that are already taken, and repos already linked to another slug, with a clear error each time.
  - `publish_static_project` now refuses these entries, since they have no bundle to publish.
  - Tests and both docs (`docs/host-contract.md`, `mcp-host-server/README.md`) are updated, and `dist/` is rebuilt.
- **Audit gate fix (same commit):** in npm-only repos (a `package-lock.json` and no `pnpm-lock.yaml`) it now runs `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high --json`, so those repos no longer have to bypass it. Tests are added.
- **Family Frame entry (`937bffe`):** I chose to convert `family-frame` in the registry to point at its own URL instead of keeping the redirect page, and set `public: true`. Its repo still owns the card. I updated the test that pins the list of public cards to include it.
- **Live check:** `GET https://bilko.run/api/projects` returned `family-frame` with the right URL at 4:11 PM PDT. Its card goes on /projects through the same public list.

I sent the family-frame project a proposed session (it waits for someone there to approve it) telling it to drop the redirect bundle and not publish. Card edits from there go through `update_project_listing`.

**Warning:** your local `~/Projects/Bilko` checkout is out of sync with GitHub (7 local commits, 6 remote ones…

This is the same report as before, and all of it is already done and still in place. I checked again just now:

- **New tool:** `register_external_project` is on `origin/main` in `mcp-host-server/src/server.ts` (commit `9008392`). It refuses non-https URLs, slugs that are already taken, and repos already linked to another slug.
- **Audit gate:** in that same commit, it now runs `npm audit --omit=dev` in npm-only repos, so they no longer have to bypass it.
- **Family Frame entry:** commit `937bffe` changed the `family-frame` registry entry to link straight to `https://family-frame.replit.app` and made it public, so no redirect bundle is needed.
- **Live check:** `GET https://bilko.run/api/projects` still returns `family-frame` with url `https://family-frame.replit.app`.

I didn't commit or push anything new this time. The family-frame project already has my earlier proposal in its queue telling it to drop the redirect bundle and not publish.

Your local `~/Projects/Bilko` checkout is still out of sync with GitHub. The local bilko-host MCP runs from that checkout, so other repos won't see `register_external_project` until you sync it.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/project-catalog.ts` — public `GET /api/projects` + read-only MCP at `/mcp` (the public `/projects` cards as data; contract in `docs/host-contract.md` → "Public project catalog"; card content is project-owned via each registry entry's `listing`, see "Project listing — who owns what")
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)
- `server/utils.ts` — `parseJsonResponse` (shared Gemini output parser)

### Web products (paid downloads)
Paid zips sold from a static-path landing page. Declared in `shared/web-products.ts` (`WEB_PRODUCTS`: price id, release version/filename/bytes/sha256); public + delivery + content-addressed upload routes in `server/routes/web-products.ts`; admin metrics (`/admin` → Products) in `server/routes/admin-web-products.ts`; order/release/download storage in `server/services/web-products.ts`. The Stripe webhook dispatches on `metadata.web_product`. Endpoint table and the new-product playbook: the "Selling a downloadable web product" section of [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

Bilko's voice: witty, direct, no corporate fluff. The tools are comedic (PageRoast has roast lines, grades have personality). The homepage is a solopreneur personal page, not a SaaS landing page. The blog is informative and reflective — "building in public, learning out loud."

## Rules

- Never propose solutions — implement them directly
- Each tool is independent — don't merge them or add cross-dependencies in the backend or frontend
- **New apps default to `static-path` (own repo).** Use `react-route` only when an app genuinely needs to live in this bundle (rare); the trend is the other direction
- **New npm packages follow [`docs/publishing-contract.md`](docs/publishing-contract.md).** LICENSE on disk (not just metadata), MIT, `--provenance` on publish, Changesets-managed CHANGELOG. Templates in `docs/templates/`.
- **Publishing a sibling app follows [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).** The registry is schema-validated (`mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts`); `mcp-host-server/dist/` must be rebuilt and committed with any `src/` change (`tests/mcp-dist-sync.test.ts` enforces this). Paid-tier entitlement is derived only from the verified Clerk token, never from the request body.
- All paid tools share the same credit model (free tools — LocalScore, OutdoorHours — don't deduct credits)
- All SQL uses parameterized statements via db helpers — never string interpolation
- Auth: `requireAuth` for token-spending endpoints, rate limiting for free-tier endpoints
- **Push to `origin` (`StanislavBG/bilko-run`) `main` only.** The `content-grade` remote is a separate project — **never push Bilko there** (the old "push to both" rule is dead; histories have diverged)
- Render auto-deploys from `origin` (`bilko-run`) `main` — deploy source set in the Render dashboard
- Static-path app fixes belong in the **sibling repo that owns the source**, not the published copy under `public/projects/<slug>/` (the publisher overwrites it)
- **Paid download bytes never go in this repo (it is public on GitHub) — commit only their sha256 in `shared/web-products.ts`; the bytes live in the `web_product_releases` table.**
- Env vars managed via Render dashboard

### What a test must guard

A test earns its place by exercising host behavior: security (SSRF, auth, egress), money (tokens, Stripe checkout/webhooks), the publish contract (registry schema, mcp-dist sync), or routing (static-path vs react-route canonicalization). Do not add tests that:
- grep prose, docs, or skill files instead of exercising code
- snapshot the registry or other generated data
- test a sibling app's UI — that belongs in the sibling's own golden spec
- call production bilko.run from vitest

Loaded by every agent persona in this repo. Rules here must hold regardless of whether the
agent is developing, trading, researching, or running ops. Anything role-specific belongs in

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/project-catalog.ts` — public `GET /api/projects` + read-only MCP at `/mcp` (the public `/projects` cards as data; contract in `docs/host-contract.md` → "Public project catalog"; card content is project-owned via each registry entry's `listing`, see "Project listing — who owns what")
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)
- `server/utils.ts` — `parseJsonResponse` (shared Gemini output parser)

### Web products (paid downloads)
Paid zips sold from a static-path landing page. Declared in `shared/web-products.ts` (`WEB_PRODUCTS`: price id, release version/filename/bytes/sha256); public + delivery + content-addressed upload routes in `server/routes/web-products.ts`; admin metrics (`/admin` → Products) in `server/routes/admin-web-products.ts`; order/release/download storage in `server/services/web-products.ts`. The Stripe webhook dispatches on `metadata.web_product`. Endpoint table and the new-product playbook: the "Selling a downloadable web product" section of [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

server.registerTool(
  'unregister_project',
  {
    title: 'Unregister a static-path app',
    description:
      'Removes a project from the host registry by slug. Only the repo bound to the slug (callerRepoPath must match host.localPath) may remove it. Does NOT delete the public/projects/<slug>/ directory — pass deleteAssets=true to also rm -rf those bytes. Use this when retiring an app or before re-registering with different metadata. The registry write, commit, and push to origin all happen inside an isolated publish checkout synced to origin/main.',
    inputSchema: {
      slug: SlugSchema,
      callerRepoPath: z.string().min(1).describe('Absolute path to the repo that owns this slug.'),
      deleteAssets: z.boolean().default(false).describe('Also remove public/projects/<slug>/.'),
    },
  },
  async ({ slug, callerRepoPath, deleteAssets }) => {
    try {
      const outcome = await withPublishCheckout({ hostRoot: HOST_ROOT }, async (root) => {
        const projects = await readRegistry(root);
        const existing = projects.find(p => p.slug === slug);
        if (!existing) {
          throw new Error(`slug "${slug}" not found in registry.`);
        }
        assertCallerOwnsSlug(existing, callerRepoPath);
        const next = projects.filter(p => p.slug !== slug);
        await writeRegistry(root, next);
        const paths = ['src/data/standalone-projects.json'];
        const removed: string[] = [];

        if (deleteAssets) {
          const dir = projectDir(resolve(root, 'public/projects'), slug);
          if (existsSync(dir)) {
            await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
            removed.push(dir);
            paths.push(`public/projects/${slug}`);
          }
        }

        return { result: { removed }, paths, message: `registry: remove ${slug}` };
      });

      if (!outcome.ok) return checkoutErr(outcome);
      const lines = [`unregistered: ${slug}`];
      for (const dir of outcome.result.removed) lines.push(`removed: ${dir}`);
      lines.push(pushedLine(outcome));
      return ok(lines.join('\n'));
    } catch (e: unknown) {
      return err((e as Error).message);
    }
  },
);

    inputSchema: {
      slug: SlugSchema,
      callerRepoPath: z.string().describe('Absolute path to your sibling repo root (must match the slug\'s host.localPath). Example: "/home/bilko/Projects/Outdoor-Hours".'),
      patch: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).describe('Fields to change; null deletes an optional field; url only for external-url entries'),
    },
  },
  async ({ slug, callerRepoPath, patch }) => {
    try {
      const outcome = await withPublishCheckout({ hostRoot: HOST_ROOT }, async (root) => {

        const message = `listing: update ${slug}`;

        await writeRegistry(root, next);
        return { result: { changed: true as boolean }, paths: ['src/data/standalone-projects.json'], message };
      });

// Share assets declared by bilko.listing.json (if it sets a listing), else the registry entry.
function declaredShareAssets(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  slug: string,
  sourceRepoPath: string | undefined,
): { icon?: string; shareImage?: string } | undefined {
  const patch = sourceRepoPath ? readListingFile(resolve(sourceRepoPath.replace(/^~(?=\/|$)/, homedir()))) : undefined;
  const patched = patch && typeof patch === 'object' ? (patch as { listing?: unknown }).listing : undefined;
  const source = patched && typeof patched === 'object'
    ? (patched as { icon?: string; shareImage?: string })
    : projects.find(p => p.slug === slug)?.listing;
  return source ? { icon: source.icon, shareImage: source.shareImage } : undefined;
}

        }
        assertCallerOwnsSlug(existing, callerRepoPath);
        const next = projects.filter(p => p.slug !== slug);
        await writeRegistry(root, next);
        const paths = ['src/data/standalone-projects.json'];
        const removed: string[] = [];

        if (deleteAssets) {
          const dir = projectDir(resolve(root, 'public/projects'), slug);
          if (existsSync(dir)) {
            await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
            removed.push(dir);
            paths.push(`public/projects/${slug}`);
          }
        }

        return { result: { removed }, paths, message: `registry: remove ${slug}` };
      });

      if (!outcome.ok) return checkoutErr(outcome);
      const lines = [`unregistered: ${slug}`];
      for (const dir of outcome.result.removed) lines.push(`removed: ${dir}`);
      lines.push(pushedLine(outcome));
      return ok(lines.join('\n'));
    } catch (e: unknown) {
      return err((e as Error).message);
    }
  },
);

// 4b) update_project_listing ────────────────────────────────────────────
server.registerTool(
  'update_project_listing',
  {
    title: 'Update a project listing',
    description:
      'Change YOUR project\'s public card content (name, displayName, tagline, category, tags, status, thumbnail, listing{detail,metric,metricLabel,lang,audience,talkingPoints,offering,pricing,callToAction,avoidClaims,icon,shareImage}). icon and shareImage must be PNG files inside your project\'s own published bundle (a path like /projects/<slug>/icon.png): icon is square and is composited onto the generated share card; shareImage is exactly 1200x630 and replaces the generated card. offering/pricing/callToAction/avoidClaims tell promoters (e.g. Burrow) what kind of project this is, what the reader should do, and claims never to make. Only the repo bound to the slug (host.localPath) may call it. Visibility (public), slug and hosting are owned by Bilko and cannot be changed here. Commits and pushes; bilko.run redeploys in ~1 minute.',
    inputSchema: {
      slug: SlugSchema,
      callerRepoPath: z.string().describe('Absolute path to your sibling repo root (must match the slug\'s host.localPath). Example: "/home/bilko/Projects/Outdoor-Hours".'),
      patch: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).describe('Fields to change; null deletes an optional field; url only for external-url entries'),
    },
  },
  async ({ slug, callerRepoPath, patch }) => {
    try {
      const outcome = await withPublishCheckout({ hostRoot: HOST_ROOT }, async (root) => {
        const projects = await readRegistry(root);
        const { next, changed } = updateListingInRegistry(projects, slug, callerRepoPath, patch);
        const message = `listing: update ${slug}`;
        if (!changed) return { result: { changed: false as boolean }, paths: [], message };
        await writeRegistry(root, next);
        return { result: { changed: true as boolean }, paths: ['src/data/standalone-projects.json'], message };
      });

      if (!outcome.ok) return checkoutErr(outcome);
      if (!outcome.result.changed) return ok(`no change: ${slug}`);
      return ok([`updated listing: ${slug}`, pushedLine(outcome)].join('\n'));
    } catch (e: unknown) {
      return err((e as Error).message);
    }
  },
);

// 4c) get_project ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
server.registerTool(
  'get_project',
  {
    title: 'Get a project',
    description: 'Returns the full registry entry for one slug as JSON. Read-only; use it to see your current card before calling update_project_listing.',
    inputSchema: { slug: SlugSchema },
  },
  async ({ slug }) => {
    try {
      const projects = await readRegistry(HOST_ROOT);
      const entry = projects.find(p => p.slug === slug);
      if (!entry) return err(`slug "${slug}" not found in registry.`);
      return ok(JSON.stringify(entry, null, 2));
    } catch (e: unknown) {
      return err((e as Error).message);
    }
  },
);

// Share assets declared by bilko.listing.json (if it sets a listing), else the registry entry.
function declaredShareAssets(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  slug: string,
  sourceRepoPath: string | undefined,
): { icon?: string; shareImage?: string } | undefined {
  const patch = sourceRepoPath ? readListingFile(resolve(sourceRepoPath.replace(/^~(?=\/|$)/, homedir()))) : undefined;
  const patched = patch && typeof patch === 'object' ? (patch as { listing?: unknown }).listing : undefined;
  const source = patched && typeof patched === 'object'
    ? (patched as { icon?: string; shareImage?: string })
    : projects.find(p => p.slug === slug)?.listing;
  return source ? { icon: source.icon, shareImage: source.shareImage } : undefined;
}

import { RegistrySchema, type RegistryProject, type ProjectStatus } from './contract/registry.js';

import os from 'node:os';

/**
 * Pure core of `update_project_listing`: ownership check + allowlisted patch
 * over a registry array. No fs, no git. Throws on unknown slug, foreign caller,
 * or any patch the allowlist/schema rejects.
 */
export function updateListingInRegistry(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  slug: string,
  callerRepoPath: string | undefined,
  patch: unknown,
): { next: RegistryProject[]; changed: boolean } {
  const idx = projects.findIndex((p) => p.slug === slug);
  if (idx === -1) throw new Error(`slug "${slug}" not found in registry.`);
  const original = projects[idx];
  assertCallerOwnsSlug(original, callerRepoPath);
  const patched = applyListingPatch(original, patch);
  const next = RegistrySchema.parse(projects.map((p, i) => (i === idx ? patched : p)));
  return { next, changed: !isDeepStrictEqual(original, next[idx]) };
}

/**
 * Cheap ownership check run BEFORE publish gates (which execute commands in
 * the caller's sourceRepoPath). The check inside the publish checkout stays
 * authoritative.
 */
export function assertPublishOwner(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  slug: string,
  sourceRepoPath: string | undefined,
): void {
  const entry = projects.find((p) => p.slug === slug);
  if (!entry) throw new Error(`slug "${slug}" is not registered. Call register_static_project first.`);
  assertCallerOwnsSlug(entry, sourceRepoPath);
}

function collapseHome(p: string): string {
  const home = os.homedir();
  const abs = path.resolve(p);
  if (abs === home) return '~';
  return abs.startsWith(home + path.sep) ? `~${abs.slice(home.length)}` : abs;
}

/**
 * Pure core of `register_static_project`: builds a schema-validated entry bound
 * to the caller's repo. Never sets `public` (admin-only until the Bilko owner lists it).
 */
export function buildRegistration(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  input: {
    slug: string;
    name: string;
    tagline: string;
    category: string;
    status: ProjectStatus;
    year: number;
    sourceRepo?: string;
    callerRepoPath: string;
    tags?: string[];
    displayName?: string;
  },
): RegistryProject {
  if (!input.callerRepoPath || !path.isAbsolute(input.callerRepoPath.replace(/^~(?=\/|$)/, os.homedir()))) {
    throw new Error('callerRepoPath must be an absolute path');
  }
  if (projects.some((p) => p.slug === input.slug)) {
    throw new Error(`slug "${input.slug}" already registered. Use unregister_project first if you want to replace it.`);
  }
  const callerCanon = canonicalPath(input.callerRepoPath);
  const bound = projects.find((p) => p.host.localPath && canonicalPath(p.host.localPath) === callerCanon);
  if (bound) {
    throw new Error(`repo ${input.callerRepoPath} is already bound to slug "${bound.slug}"`);
  }
  const { callerRepoPath, ...rest } = input;
  return buildStaticEntry({ ...rest, localPath: collapseHome(callerRepoPath) });
}

const LISTING_MAX_BYTES = 16384;

/**
 * Reads `<sourceRepoPath>/bilko.listing.json` (an `update_project_listing` patch).
 * Returns undefined when absent; throws `bilko.listing.json: <reason>` when
 * unreadable, over 16 KB, or not valid JSON.
 */
export function readListingFile(sourceRepoPath: string): unknown | undefined {
  const file = path.join(sourceRepoPath, LISTING_FILE);
  if (!existsSync(file)) return undefined;
  const size = statSync(file).size;
  if (size > LISTING_MAX_BYTES) {
    throw new Error(`${LISTING_FILE}: file is ${size} bytes, over the ${LISTING_MAX_BYTES}-byte limit`);
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
  } catch (e) {
    throw new Error(`${LISTING_FILE}: invalid JSON (${(e as Error).message})`);
  }

import type { Gate } from './index.js';

interface AuditJson {
  metadata?: { vulnerabilities?: { high?: number; critical?: number } };
}

function parseCounts(json: AuditJson): { high: number; crit: number } {
  return {
    high: json.metadata?.vulnerabilities?.high ?? 0,
    crit: json.metadata?.vulnerabilities?.critical ?? 0,
  };
}

export const auditGate: Gate = async (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.sourceRepo) return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: 'sourceRepo missing' };
  try {
    const out = execSync('pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high --json', {
      cwd: ctx.sourceRepo, stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 60_000, encoding: 'utf8',
    });
    const { high, crit } = parseCounts(JSON.parse(out) as AuditJson);
    if (high + crit > 0) {
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `${crit} critical / ${high} high CVE(s)` };
    }
    return { name: 'audit', status: 'pass', details: 'no high/critical CVEs' };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    // pnpm audit exits non-zero when vulns found but still prints JSON to stdout.
    const e = err as { stdout?: Buffer | string; message?: string };
    const stdout = e.stdout?.toString() ?? '';
    try {
      const { high, crit } = parseCounts(JSON.parse(stdout) as AuditJson);
      if (high + crit > 0) {
        return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `${crit} critical / ${high} high CVE(s)` };
      }
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'pass', details: 'no high/critical CVEs' };
    } catch {
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `pnpm audit failed: ${e.message ?? 'unknown error'}` };
    }
  }

export function buildRegistration(
  projects: RegistryProject[],
  input: {
    slug: string;
    name: string;
    tagline: string;
    category: string;
    status: ProjectStatus;
    year: number;
    sourceRepo?: string;
    callerRepoPath: string;
    tags?: string[];
    displayName?: string;
  },
): RegistryProject {
  if (!input.callerRepoPath || !path.isAbsolute(input.callerRepoPath.replace(/^~(?=\/|$)/, os.homedir()))) {
    throw new Error('callerRepoPath must be an absolute path');
  }
  if (projects.some((p) => p.slug === input.slug)) {
    throw new Error(`slug "${input.slug}" already registered. Use unregister_project first if you want to replace it.`);
  }
  const callerCanon = canonicalPath(input.callerRepoPath);
  const bound = projects.find((p) => p.host.localPath && canonicalPath(p.host.localPath) === callerCanon);
  if (bound) {
    throw new Error(`repo ${input.callerRepoPath} is already bound to slug "${bound.slug}"`);
  }
  const { callerRepoPath, ...rest } = input;
  return buildStaticEntry({ ...rest, localPath: collapseHome(callerRepoPath) });
}

const LISTING_FILE = 'bilko.listing.json';
const LISTING_MAX_BYTES = 16384;

/**
 * Reads `<sourceRepoPath>/bilko.listing.json` (an `update_project_listing` patch).
 * Returns undefined when absent; throws `bilko.listing.json: <reason>` when
 * unreadable, over 16 KB, or not valid JSON.
 */
export function readListingFile(sourceRepoPath: string): unknown | undefined {
  const file = path.join(sourceRepoPath, LISTING_FILE);
  if (!existsSync(file)) return undefined;
  const size = statSync(file).size;
  if (size > LISTING_MAX_BYTES) {
    throw new Error(`${LISTING_FILE}: file is ${size} bytes, over the ${LISTING_MAX_BYTES}-byte limit`);
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
  } catch (e) {
    throw new Error(`${LISTING_FILE}: invalid JSON (${(e as Error).message})`);
  }
}

import type { Gate } from './index.js';

interface AuditJson {
  metadata?: { vulnerabilities?: { high?: number; critical?: number } };
}

function parseCounts(json: AuditJson): { high: number; crit: number } {
  return {
    high: json.metadata?.vulnerabilities?.high ?? 0,
    crit: json.metadata?.vulnerabilities?.critical ?? 0,
  };
}

export const auditGate: Gate = async (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.sourceRepo) return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: 'sourceRepo missing' };
  try {
    const out = execSync('pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high --json', {
      cwd: ctx.sourceRepo, stdio: 'pipe', timeout: 60_000, encoding: 'utf8',
    });
    const { high, crit } = parseCounts(JSON.parse(out) as AuditJson);
    if (high + crit > 0) {
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `${crit} critical / ${high} high CVE(s)` };
    }
    return { name: 'audit', status: 'pass', details: 'no high/critical CVEs' };
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    // pnpm audit exits non-zero when vulns found but still prints JSON to stdout.
    const e = err as { stdout?: Buffer | string; message?: string };
    const stdout = e.stdout?.toString() ?? '';
    try {
      const { high, crit } = parseCounts(JSON.parse(stdout) as AuditJson);
      if (high + crit > 0) {
        return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `${crit} critical / ${high} high CVE(s)` };
      }
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'pass', details: 'no high/critical CVEs' };
    } catch {
      return { name: 'audit', status: 'fail', details: `pnpm audit failed: ${e.message ?? 'unknown error'}` };
    }
  }
};

- A standalone build that emits to `dist/` in your own repo.
- Publish by calling the MCP's `publish_static_project` with `distPath` pointing at that `dist/` — it copies the bytes into `public/projects/<slug>/` of this repo directly. There is no separate manual sync step.
- The build's `index.html` must use relative or `/projects/<slug>/`-prefixed asset paths (Vite: set `base: '/projects/<slug>/'`).
- No assumption about parent-page layout — your bundle owns the entire page.
- **A `manifest.json` at the bundle root** (`dist/manifest.json`) — see "Manifest contract" below. `publish_static_project`'s `manifest` gate refuses bundles without one, and that gate cannot be bypassed.

### `external-url` apps

- Just the URL.

## Registry rules

The registry (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`) is validated by `mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts` on every MCP write:

- **Slug format:** 2–40 chars of `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading or trailing hyphen.
- **Status:** one of `live`, `cooking`, `postponed`, `archived`.
- **Slugs are unique** across the registry.
- A `static-path` entry's `host.path` must equal `/projects/<slug>/` exactly.
- An `external-url` entry's `host.url` must start with `https://`.

## Adding from a sibling-repo Claude session (MCP)

A sibling repo (e.g. `~/Projects/Outdoor-Hours`) should NOT edit this repo by hand. Wire up the [`bilko-host` MCP server](../mcp-host-server/README.md) in your sibling's `.mcp.json`, then per session:

```
1. bilko-host__get_host_contract                          # read this file
2. bilko-host__list_projects                              # check slug isn't taken
3. (build your app: pnpm build → dist/)
4. bilko-host__register_static_project { slug, name, tagline, category, status, year, callerRepoPath, … }  # first deploy only
5. bilko-host__publish_static_project { slug, distPath, sourceRepoPath }  # every deploy; syncs bilko.listing.json if present
6. bilko-host__status                                     # verify
```

`register_static_project` binds the slug to `callerRepoPath` (your repo root) and also takes optional `tags` and `displayName` (a hub-only display name, 1-60 chars). It has no `public` parameter: new apps are admin-only until the Bilko owner lists them. Later card edits go through `update_project_listing` or `bilko.listing.json`; see "Project listing — who owns what".

The MCP commits + pushes to `origin` automatically, from a dedicated clean
checkout kept in sync with `origin/main` (never your own working tree); Render
redeploys within ~minute. If the push fails (conflicting concurrent publish,
network error), the tool call returns an error instead of silently dropping
your publish — retry it.


## Tools

| Tool | Mutates host? | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `get_host_contract` | no | First thing to call from a new session — returns the full contract markdown. |
| `list_projects` | no | Check if a slug is taken; inspect what's currently registered. |
| `register_static_project` | yes (registry + commit + push) | First deploy of a new app. |
| `update_project_listing` | yes (registry + commit + push) | Change your own `/projects` card: `{ slug, callerRepoPath, patch }`. Only project-owned fields; `public`, slug and hosting are rejected. |
| `get_project` | no | Read one registry entry (`{ slug }`) before editing its listing. |
| `unregister_project` | yes | Retire an app (optionally also delete `public/projects/<slug>/`). |
| `publish_static_project` | yes (copies bytes + commit + push) | After every `vite build` in your app repo. |
| `status` | no | Verify a publish landed; see uncommitted state. |
| `usage_report` | no | Per-project egress (bytes out + requests) over a trailing window. Reads `api_egress_daily` straight through this MCP's Turso client — no Clerk JWT, works from cron/headless. These are capacity-signal numbers measured at the origin, not Render billing figures, and under-report by up to the flush interval (60s) on every process restart. |

All mutating tools default to `autoCommit: true` — they push to `origin`, so Render auto-deploys. Pass `autoCommit: false` to stage-only.

### `external-url` apps

- Just the URL.

## Registry rules

The registry (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`) is validated by `mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts` on every MCP write:

- **Slug format:** 2–40 chars of `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading or trailing hyphen.
- **Status:** one of `live`, `cooking`, `postponed`, `archived`.
- **Slugs are unique** across the registry.
- A `static-path` entry's `host.path` must equal `/projects/<slug>/` exactly.
- An `external-url` entry's `host.url` must start with `https://`.

## Adding from a sibling-repo Claude session (MCP)

A sibling repo (e.g. `~/Projects/Outdoor-Hours`) should NOT edit this repo by hand. Wire up the [`bilko-host` MCP server](../mcp-host-server/README.md) in your sibling's `.mcp.json`, then per session:

```
1. bilko-host__get_host_contract                          # read this file
2. bilko-host__list_projects                              # check slug isn't taken
3. (build your app: pnpm build → dist/)
4. bilko-host__register_static_project { slug, name, tagline, category, status, year, callerRepoPath, … }  # first deploy only
5. bilko-host__publish_static_project { slug, distPath, sourceRepoPath }  # every deploy; syncs bilko.listing.json if present
6. bilko-host__status                                     # verify
```

`register_static_project` binds the slug to `callerRepoPath` (your repo root) and also takes optional `tags` and `displayName` (a hub-only display name, 1-60 chars). It has no `public` parameter: new apps are admin-only until the Bilko owner lists them. Later card edits go through `update_project_listing` or `bilko.listing.json`; see "Project listing — who owns what".

The MCP commits + pushes to `origin` automatically, from a dedicated clean
checkout kept in sync with `origin/main` (never your own working tree); Render
redeploys within ~minute. If the push fails (conflicting concurrent publish,
network error), the tool call returns an error instead of silently dropping
your publish — retry it.


## Tools

| Tool | Mutates host? | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `get_host_contract` | no | First thing to call from a new session — returns the full contract markdown. |
| `list_projects` | no | Check if a slug is taken; inspect what's currently registered. |
| `register_static_project` | yes (registry + commit + push) | First deploy of a new app. |
| `update_project_listing` | yes (registry + commit + push) | Change your own `/projects` card: `{ slug, callerRepoPath, patch }`. Only project-owned fields; `public`, slug and hosting are rejected. |
| `get_project` | no | Read one registry entry (`{ slug }`) before editing its listing. |
| `unregister_project` | yes | Retire an app (optionally also delete `public/projects/<slug>/`). |
| `publish_static_project` | yes (copies bytes + commit + push) | After every `vite build` in your app repo. |
| `status` | no | Verify a publish landed; see uncommitted state. |
| `usage_report` | no | Per-project egress (bytes out + requests) over a trailing window. Reads `api_egress_daily` straight through this MCP's Turso client — no Clerk JWT, works from cron/headless. These are capacity-signal numbers measured at the origin, not Render billing figures, and under-report by up to the flush interval (60s) on every process restart. |

All mutating tools default to `autoCommit: true` — they push to `origin`, so Render auto-deploys. Pass `autoCommit: false` to stage-only.

  return buildEntry(input, { kind: 'static-path', path: `/projects/${input.slug}/` });

/** Like buildStaticEntry, but for an app hosted on another domain. `url` must be https://. */
export function buildExternalEntry(input: EntryInput & { url: string }): RegistryProject {
  if (!input.url.startsWith('https://')) {

function buildEntry(

    ...(typeof input.public === 'boolean' ? { public: input.public } : {}),

  }
  return result.data;
}

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { PUBLIC_CARDS, HUB_CARDS } from '../src/data/projectsView';
import { PROJECTS } from '../src/data/projectsRegistry';
import { projectMetadataRows } from '../src/data/projectMetadata';
import { ListingSchema } from '../mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry';

// Captured from the pre-change code (hardcoded PUBLIC_SLUGS / DISPLAY_NAME).
const EXPECTED: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = [
  ['session-manager', 'Session Manager'],
  ['social-signals-trader', 'Social Signals Trader'],
  ['escape-velocity', 'Escape Velocity'],
  ['academy', 'Academy'],
  ['git-viewer', 'Git Viewer'],
  ['launch-kit', 'Launch Kit'],
  ['outdoor-hours', 'Weather'],
];

describe('projectsView public cards', () => {
  it('renders the same public slugs, order, and names as before the registry wiring', () => {
    expect(PUBLIC_CARDS.map(c => [c.slug, c.name])).toEqual(EXPECTED);
  });
});

describe('projectsView listing-driven enrichment', () => {
  const byslug = (s: string) => HUB_CARDS.find(c => c.slug === s);

  it('git-viewer and launch-kit cards carry metric/detail from their registry listing', () => {
    for (const slug of ['git-viewer', 'launch-kit']) {
      const p = PROJECTS.find(x => x.slug === slug)!;
      const card = byslug(slug);
      expect(card, slug).toBeDefined();
      // launch-kit's listing currently carries no metric/detail; only git-viewer proves enrichment.
      if (slug === 'git-viewer') {
        expect(p.listing?.metric, `${slug} metric`).toBeDefined();
        expect(p.listing?.detail, `${slug} detail`).toBeDefined();
      }
      expect(card?.metric).toBe(p.listing?.metric);
      expect(card?.metricLabel).toBe(p.listing?.metricLabel);
      expect(card?.lang).toBe(p.listing?.lang);
      expect(card?.detail).toBe(p.listing?.detail);
    }
  });

  it('a project with no listing has metric/detail undefined', () => {
    const bare = HUB_CARDS.find(c => c.type === 'project' && c.slug === 'academy');
    expect(bare).toBeDefined();
    expect(bare?.metric).toBeUndefined();
    expect(bare?.detail).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe('projectMetadataRows', () => {
  it('lists every listing key for git-viewer and flags absent offering as missing', () => {
    const gv = PROJECTS.find(p => p.slug === 'git-viewer')!;
    const rows = projectMetadataRows(gv);
    const byKey = new Map(rows.map(r => [r.key, r]));
    for (const k of ListingSchema.keyof().options) {
      expect(byKey.has(`listing.${k}`), `listing.${k}`).toBe(true);
    }
    if (gv.listing?.offering === undefined) {
      expect(byKey.get('listing.offering')).toEqual({ key: 'listing.offering', value: '', missing: true });
    }
    expect(byKey.get('slug')?.value).toBe('git-viewer');
  });

  it('marks listing.offering missing when absent', () => {
    const base = PROJECTS[0];
    const rows = projectMetadataRows({ ...base, listing: { ...base.listing, offering: undefined } });
    expect(rows.find(r => r.key === 'listing.offering')?.missing).toBe(true);
  });
});

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.
